questions.question: Which value among sqrt[3]{5},sqrt[4]{6}, sqrt[6]{{12}},sqrt[{12}]{{276}} is the largest?
questions.solution:
Firstly, we have to find the L.C.M. of all the powers so that we can equate the bases.

L.C.M. of 3, 4, 6, 12 = 12

⇒ (5)¹/³ = (5⁴)¹/¹² = (625)¹/¹²

⇒ (6)¹/⁴ = (6³)¹/¹² = (216)¹/¹²

⇒ (12)¹/⁶ = (12²)¹/¹² = (144)¹/¹²

⇒ (276)¹/¹²

Since, the powers are equal, we can equate the bases

Hence, (5)¹/³ is the largest

questions.question: A piece of work was finished by A, B and C together. A and B together finished 60% of the work and B and C together finished 70% of the work. Who among the three is most efficient?
questions.solution:
Let the total amount of work be a

⇒ Work done by A and B together = 0.6a

⇒ Work done by C alone = a – 0.6a = 0.4a

⇒ Work done by B and C together = 0.7a

⇒ Work done by B alone = 0.7a – 0.4a = 0.3a

⇒ Work done by A alone = a – 0.7a = 0.3a

∴ the most efficient is C

questions.question: The marked price of a sofa set is Rs 4800 which is sold at Rs 3672 at two successive discounts. If the first discount is 10%, then what will be the second discount (in %)?
questions.solution:
Marked Price = Rs. 4800

Selling price = 3672

⇒ Total discount = MP – SP = Rs. 1128

Price after first discount = 4800 – 4800 x (10/100) = Rs. 4320

Second discount = [(4320 – 3672)/4320] x 100 = 15%

∴ the second discount = 15%

A : B : C = 3 : 4 : 5

Interest rates -

For A, B, and C = 20%, 15%, and 10%

questions.question: The average age of 120 members of a society is 60.7 years. By addition of 30 new members, the average age becomes 56.3 years. What is the average age (in years) of newly joined members?
questions.solution:
Given: Number of members earlier = 120

⇒ Total age of all the members earlier = 120 x 60.7 = 7284 …..(i)

⇒ Total age of all the members presently = 150 x 56.3 = 8445 …..(ii)

⇒ Total age of new members = (ii) – (I)

⇒ 8445 – 7284 = 1161

∴ Average age of newly joined members = 1161/30 = 38.7

questions.question: By selling 175 pineapples, the gain is equal to the selling price of 50 pineapples. What is the gain percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the selling price of 1 apple be a

⇒ S.P. of 175 pineapples = 175a

⇒ gain = 50a

⇒ Cost price = 175a – 50a = 125a

∴ gain percent = [50a/125a] x 100 = 40 %

questions.question: If A has got 20% more marks than B, then by what percent marks of B are less than the marks of A?
questions.solution:
Let the marks of B be c

⇒ marks of A = c (1 + 0.2) = 1.2c

Now, required percent = (marks of A –marks of B) /marks of A

∴ required percent = [(1.2c – c)/1.2c] x 100 = 100c/6c = 16.66%

questions.question: A train leaves Delhi at 10 a.m. and reaches Jaipur at 4 p.m. on same day. Another train leaves Jaipur at 12 p.m. and reaches Delhi at 5 p.m. on same day. What is the time of day (approximately) when the two trains will meet?
questions.solution:
Let the total distance between Delhi and Jaipur be a

Travel time of train A going from Delhi to Jaipur = 4 p.m – 10 a.m = 6 hours

⇒ Speed of train A = a/6 km/hr

Travel time of train B going from Jaipur to Delhi = 5 p.m – 12 p.m = 5 hours

⇒ Speed of train B = a/5 km/hr

⇒ Distance covered by train A in 2 hours = (a/6) x 2 = a/3

Distance left for train A to cover when time is 12 : 00 pm = a – a/3 = 2a/3

Relative velocity for train A w.r.t B = a/6 + a/5 = 11a/30

⇒ Time Taken = Distance/speed= (2a/3)/(11a/30) = 20/11 hours

∴ required time = 12 : 00 pm + 20/11 hours = 1 : 49 pm

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest compounding half yearly for 1 year and the simple interest for 1 year on a certain sum of money lent out at 8% per annum is Rs 64. What is the sum (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Calculating compound interest = P(1 + 0.04) ² – P

Calculating simple interest = P x 0.08 x 1

⇒ P(1 + 0.04) ² – P – (P x 0.08 x 1) = 64

⇒ P(1.04) ² – 1.08P = 64

⇒ (1.0816 – 1.08) P = 64

⇒ P = 64/0.0016

⇒ P = 40000

questions.question: If (x – 2) and (x + 3) are the factors of the equation x² + k₁x + k₂ = 0, then what are the values of k₁ and k₂?
questions.solution:
Given: (x – 2) and (x + 3) are factors

⇒ Roots of the equation = 2, -3

Putting x = 2 in the given equation, we get

⇒ 2² + 2k₁ + k₂ = 0

⇒ 2k₁ + k₂ = - 4 …..(i)

Similarly, Putting x = -3 in the given equation, we get

⇒ (-3) ² - 3k₁ + k₂ = 0

⇒ - 3k₁ + k₂ = -9 ……(ii)

Subtracting (i) and (ii)

⇒ 5k₁ = 5

⇒ k₁ = 1

Putting value of k₁ in (i)

⇒ k₂ = -6

∴ k₁ = 1 and k₂ = -6

questions.question: If x – y – √18 = -1 and x + y – 3√2 = 1, what is the value of 12xy(x² – y²)?
questions.solution:
Given: x – y = –1 + √18 ----(i)

⇒ x + y = 1 + 3√2 ----(ii)

Multiplying (i) and (ii) . We get

⇒ x² – y² = (–1 + √18) (1 + 3√2)

⇒ x² – y² = -1 + 18 = 17

Now, from (i) and (ii)

⇒ x = 3√2 and y = 1

So, 12xy = 12(3√2) = 36√2

∴ Required value = 12xy(x² – y²) = (36√2) (17) = 612√2

questions.question: If p/q = r/s = t/u = √5, then what is the value of [(3p² + 4r² + 5t²) /(3q² + 4s² + 5u²) ]?
questions.solution:
Here, p = √5q

⇒ r = √5s

⇒ t = √5u

Now, substituting above values in required value

⇒ [(3(√5q) ² + 4(√5s) ² + 5(√5u) ²) /(3q² + 4s² + 5u²) ]

⇒ 5[(3q² + 4s² + 5u²)/(3q² + 4s² + 5u²) ]

∴ answer is 5

BD = BC - CD = 9 - 3 = 6cm

questions.question: In triangle PQR, A is the point of intersection of all the altitudes and B is the point of intersection of all the angle bisectors of the triangle. If ∠PBR = 105°, then what is the value of ∠PAR (in degrees)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In ΔPQR, A is the point of intersection of all the altitudes.

B is the point of intersection of all the angle bisectors of the triangle.

∠PBR = 105°

**Calculation:**

Let PX, QY, and RZ be the angle bisectors

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/457a4414039d8a913b92e1cf7ffdfa3f7b84f605ecfa7e0f3700353ec31d7b9c.png] 

In ΔPBR

⇒ ∠BPY + ∠BRY + 105° = 180°

⇒ ∠BPY + ∠BRY = 180° - 105° = 75°

Now, this sum is half of ∠P and ∠R

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 75° x 2 = 150°

In ΔPQR

∠Q = 180° - 150° = 30°

Let PM, QN, and RO be the altitudes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f490648bed36a5280171245fc74c027f97b610c5ce616871c201a84c388b6cf1.png] 

In ΔRQO

⇒ ∠QRO + ∠RZO + ∠Q = 180°

⇒ ∠QRO = 180° – 90° – 30°

⇒ ∠QRO = 60°

In ΔAMR

⇒ ∠MAR = 180° – 90° - 60°

⇒ ∠MAR = 30°

Now, ∠PAR + ∠MAR = 180°

⇒ ∠PAR = 180° – 30° = 150°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** ∠Q/2 + 90 = ∠PBR

⇒ ∠Q/2 + 90° = 105° 

⇒ ∠Q = 30°

Now, A is the orthocenter.

∠Q + ∠PAR = 180° 

⇒ 30° + ∠PAR = 180° 

∠PAR = 150° 

∴ ∠PAR is 150°.

questions.question: If there are 4 lines in a plane, then what cannot be the number of points of intersection of these lines?
questions.solution:
**Given:-**

4 lines in a plane

**Formula used:-**

Max. Number of intersections = n(n – 1)/2,

where n is the number of lines

**Calculation:-**

Put n = 4

Max. number of intersections = 4(3)/2 = 6

So, an option having a value greater than 6, cannot be possible.

Hence, 7 can't be the number of points of intersection.

questions.question: If Mr. Raghav taught a total of 500 hours, then what is the difference in number of hours of teaching algebra and modern Maths?
questions.solution:
Number of hours dedicated to algebra = (9/100) x 500 = 45 hours

Number of hours dedicated to modern maths = (4/100) x 500 = 20 hours

∴ difference in number of hours of teaching algebra and modern Maths = 45 – 20 = 25 hours.

questions.question: Mr. Raghav taught Geometry for 36 hours. If the time taken in teaching Ratio consitutes one-fourth of the time for Arithmetic, then for how much time (in hours) did he taught the topic of Ratio?
questions.solution:
Number of hours dedicated to geometry = 36 hours

Since, 36 hours is 6% of the total hours taught

⇒ 1% of total hours = 36/6 = 6 hours

⇒ Total hours = 6 x 100 = 600 hours

Number of hours dedicated to arithmetic = (46/100) (600) = 276 hours

∴ Number of hours dedicated to ratio = 276/4 = 69 hours

questions.question: If Data Interpretation and Modern Maths were taught for a combined time of 96 hours, then for how much time (in hours) were Number system and Geometry taught?
questions.solution:
% of time dedicated to Data Interpretation and Modern Maths = 8 + 4 = 12%

⇒ Given : 12% of total hours = 96 hours

⇒ 1% of total hours = 96/12 = 8hours

Hence, total hours = 8 x 100 = 800 hours

⇒ % time dedicated to Number system and Geometry taught = 23 + 6 = 29%

So, total hours dedicated to Number system and Geometry = 800 x (29/100) = 232 hrs

∴ answer is 232 hours

questions.question: A new topic named Problem Solving was also introduced and it was decided that 10% time of all topics except Arithmetic will be devoted to it. What will be the central angle (in degrees) made by Problem Solving in the new pie chart?
questions.solution:
% left after removing arithmetic = 100 – 46 = 54%

⇒ 10% of the left percentage is dedicated to problem solving

⇒ % dedicated to problem solving = (10/100) x 54 = 5.4%

∴ the central angle = (5.4/100) x 360° = 19.44°
